chunks: Dhibyān (ibn Ḥukaym ibn al-Awdī, Abū ʿAmr). His affair is confused.

key_terms.أَمَرُهُ: His affair/status, referring to his reliability in narration
key_terms.مُخْتَلِطٌ: Confused or mixed, indicating uncertain reliability

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when a narrator's 'amru' is described as mukhtalit in Shia hadith sciences?
ai.summary: This is a biographical note on the narrator Dhibyān ibn Ḥukaym ibn al-Awdī, known as Abū ʿAmr. It states that his 'affair' (amaru) is confused, a technical term in ʿIlm al-Rijāl indicating that his status as a reliable narrator is mixed or uncertain, meaning he is neither clearly trustworthy nor clearly weak.
